spec_match.rationale: Demonstrates the WebIDL enum contract that governs this feature's rollout: unknown values for a known dictionary member throw TypeError at conversion (webidl #idl-enums), unknown members are silently dropped, and enum matching is case-sensitive — each shown with real calls against the four accepting surfaces.

interactive.rationale: Five toggle buttons probe curated values (both new ones, wrong case, a bogus string, and rec2100-linear which chromestatus explicitly excludes from this feature) against all four surfaces with verbatim browser messages; a getter-probe button measures whether the dictionary member is read at all.

blurb_alignment.rationale: The index card promises real TypeError messages plus the silently-ignored failure mode and the it-didn't-throw fallacy, which is precisely the page's two stages.

edge_cases.rationale: This page IS the edge-case angle: rejection, silent substitution, case sensitivity, a future enum value, and the measured 141 detail that the two new values throw differently shaped messages (one runtime-gated, one absent from the enum) are all covered and re-measurable on the visitor's browser.

references.rationale: See-also links chromestatus.com/feature/5122501071994880, WebIDL enumeration types, the HTML spec enum, and the sibling matrix concept.

conformance.rationale: The feature suite includes baseline-unknown-value-rejected (kind: throws) pinning the bogus-value contract this page demonstrates, alongside the positive readback assertions.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Headless Chromium 141 via CDP: all five value buttons and the getter probe clicked at 1280×2000 and 360×1600; the load-time probe rendered 'supported on 0, rejected on 4' for srgb-linear with the verbatim TypeError text per surface; getter probe reported the member is read; zero console errors; post-interaction screenshots read on both classes.

telemetry_health.rationale: Asserts gate-probe-ran per probe with the observed state vector, gate-bogus-never-supported (a made-up value must never read back as itself), and gate-getter-probe-ran with the memberRead result.

design_system.rationale: CSS variables only; the pressed toggle state overrides background and color together (accent-blue on ivory, 4.6:1); verdict colours sit on near-white; the results table scrolls in its own container.

accessibility.rationale: The value pickers are native buttons in a named group with aria-pressed state, outcomes are announced through aria-live outputs, table headers carry scope, and verdicts are words (supported/rejected/ignored) rather than colour alone.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: Verified at 360×1600 DPR3 and 1280×2000: button row wraps, the message table scrolls internally with overflow-wrap on long TypeError strings, no page-level horizontal overflow, 44px targets.

openQuestions.title: Re-measure the two-rejections comparison on Chrome 152-154 builds
openQuestions.detail: The 'two rejections are not the same rejection' section records Chromium 141's message shapes (srgb-linear enum-present-but-gated vs display-p3-linear enum-absent). Intermediate builds may move display-p3-linear into the gated state, making both messages match; the copy says 'can differ' and defers to the visitor's own table, but re-measuring on a 152+ build would let it date the transition precisely.

guidanceConsulted.query: toggle button group aria-pressed state announcements
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Expose exclusive-choice button groups with aria-pressed and a group label, and announce resulting state changes through live regions.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: The picker is a role=group with aria-label; exactly one button holds aria-pressed=true; each probe writes its outcome sentence to output[aria-live=polite].

guidanceConsulted.query: responsive control panel without horizontal overflow
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Wrap control rows with flex-wrap and give long monospaced strings overflow-wrap so error messages cannot widen the page.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Buttons wrap; td.mono uses overflow-wrap:anywhere for the long TypeError messages; measured 0px page overflow at 360px.

summary: Edge/failure angle, and the page that encodes this project's own anti-regression lesson: enum rejection, silent member-dropping, and case sensitivity demonstrated with live calls and verbatim messages, plus a getter probe separating 'browser rejects the value' from 'browser never reads the member' — the two failure modes a naive try/catch conflates.
